content:
I didn't find this lesson in a courtroom
I found it in a plant nursery.

Look around.

Some plants are flourishing.

Some are still waiting for the right pot

Some haven't even been planted yet

The law isn't very different.

A startup with no founders' agreement, A business with no written contract, A partnership built only on trust.

They may survive for a while

But without the right legal foundation, growth becomes a matter of luck not strategy

The strongest tree doesn't grow because it's lucky

It grows because its roots are protected

Businesses work the same way

Most legal disputes don't begin with bad intentions

They begin with assumptions.

We'll figure it out later
We know each other
We don't need paperwork

By the time a lawyer gets involved the problem has usually been growing quietly for months.

The best legal work is often invisible.

It's the dispute that never happened the partnership that never broke. The business that kept growing because someone took legal protection seriously from day one.

Just like these plants, every business deserves the right environment to grow.

And good law creates that environment.

What's one legal mistake you've seen businesses make that could have been avoided with a single document?
